scene1_screen1.text: Julie stepped into her parents’ house expecting food, wine, and no mention of her love life. Well. Two out of three wasn’t bad.

scene1_screen2.text: She shook snow from her coat, kicked off her boots—

scene1_screen3.text: (outside the room, sing-song) Julie! Come quick — look who’s here!

scene1_screen4.text: Julie froze. That tone was never good news. That tone meant drama. That tone meant—

scene1_screen5.text: Patrick. Her ex. The one who once brought her soup when she was sick, then ghosted her the week after celebrating July 4th.

scene1_screen6.text: The one who annotated the margins of her favorite book in pen. Leaning against the fireplace now, like a man with no concept of emotional landmines — or how close he was to stepping on one.

scene1_screen7.text: He held a mug of cocoa like it was a peace offering from a minor war crime. His smile? Casual. Dangerous. Smug. The same one he wore when he said, “Technically, we were on a break.”

scene1_screen8.text: (lightly) Hey, Jules. Happy Almost New Year?

scene1_screen9.text: (ooutside the room, crunching cashews) He brought wine!

scene1_screen11.text: (dryly) Nothing says “emotional ambush” like a Pinot Noir.

scene1_screen12.text: Julie stared at Patrick like he might explode. He just gave her that lopsided smile — the one that got him out of so many arguments and into so many regrets.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen1.text: Alright. Let’s act like two adults and not the blooper reel of a Netflix romance.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen2.text: She marched past him into the kitchen, grabbed two wine glasses, and handed him one like it was part of a hostage exchange.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen4.text: More like armed neutrality. Expires at midnight.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen1.text: (with a tight smile) What a surprise. Dropping in unannounced. How very... on brand.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen2.text: (grinning) Your mom said it’d be “low-key and emotionally healing.”

scene1_choice1_option2_screen3.text: Ah. Nothing says healing like unresolved trauma under twinkle lights.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen4.text: She sipped her wine with the grace of a woman who'd survived three family dinners and a broken engagement.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen1.text: (to her mom) You invited my ex to New Year’s dinner?

scene1_choice1_option3_screen2.text: We just thought… You two were magic. Like in that one movie!

scene1_choice1_option3_screen3.text: (from the couch) The one where they hate each other but kiss in the snow. I like that one.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen4.text: You mean the one with the restraining order?

scene1_choice1_option3_screen6.text: Julie pinched the bridge of her nose. Mariah Carey started playing softly from the Bluetooth speaker. Of course she did.

scene1_screen13.text: Patrick took a step closer, less smug now, more… uncertain.

scene1_screen14.text: (quietly) For what it’s worth… I didn’t know you’d be here either. But... I don’t hate seeing you.

scene1_screen15.text: Julie didn’t answer. She did, however, top off her glass. Generously.

scene2_screen1.text: Julie sat cross-legged on the carpet in front of the tree, swirling the last drops of mulled wine in her glass. Patrick sat a cushion’s width away, trying to open a tin of homemade cookies with the same energy one usually reserves for defusing bombs.

scene2_screen2.text: (straining) Is this tin childproof or heartbreak-proof?

scene2_screen3.text: (dry) Both. My mom's passive-aggressive like that.

scene2_screen4.text: The tree lights flickered gently as if also judging him. Finally, the lid popped off violently. A rogue gingerbread man flew out and hit the side of Julie’s forehead. She blinked.

scene2_screen5.text: …It was aiming for my dignity. You just got in the way.

scene2_screen6.text: (mock solemn) I’ll carry the scar forever.

scene2_screen7.text: She broke the cookie in half and handed him a piece. Their fingers brushed. It didn’t feel like fire. It felt… familiar.

scene2_screen8.text: (quietly) Do you remember the year your dad tried to deep-fry a turkey and blacked out the whole block?

scene2_screen9.text: Yes. You came over with pizza. My mom thought that meant you were proposing.

scene2_screen11.text: (laughing) You winked. You winked at my dad.

scene2_screen12.text: They laughed, full and real. The kind of laugh that warmed even the burnt edges of memory. Then the silence settled. Not awkward. Just heavy with the weight of everything unspoken.

opts.text: Try to make her laugh again

scene2_choice1_option1_screen1.text: I messed it up, Julie. I thought I had to have everything figured out before I could love you right. But honestly? I just had to show up.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen2.text: Julie didn’t say anything at first. Just looked at him — not mad, not nostalgic. Just seeing him. Present tense.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen3.text: (softly) It wasn’t all your fault. I slammed a few doors too.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen1.text: (grinning) Okay, but — be honest — my gingerbread man throwing arm? Still impressive, right?

scene2_choice1_option2_screen2.text: I’ll admit, I felt mildly threatened.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen3.text: We could go pro. Competitive cookie combat.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen4.text: Team name: The Emotional Baggage Handlers.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen5.text: They doubled over laughing again. Somewhere upstairs, a relative snored in approval.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen1.text: I didn’t expect this to feel so... easy. Or that just sitting next to you would still feel like home.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen2.text: Julie turned her head slowly. The tree lights danced in her eyes.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen3.text: (soft, with a smile) It’s not easy. It’s just familiar. Big difference.

scene2_screen13.text: The clock ticked past 11 PM. The house was quiet now — muffled, as if even time had slowed down to eavesdrop.

scene2_screen14.text: Somewhere upstairs, a floorboard creaked. Then a muffled voice — Julie’s mom, unmistakably stage-whispering:

scene2_screen15.text: (outside the room) No one goes in the living room! I repeat — do not ruin the tension!

scene2_screen16.text: Then came her dad’s proud whisper: “Like watching a nature documentary. Two exes. One habitat.”

scene2_screen17.text: Julie blinked. Patrick chuckled under his breath.

scene2_screen18.text: You know we can hear you, right?

scene2_screen19.text: (outside the room) Oh, we know, sweetheart. That’s the point.

scene2_screen20.text: Julie leaned back on her palms, looking at the twinkling ornaments, then at him.

scene2_screen22.text: (instantly) Your uncle’s karaoke version of “Santa Baby.”

scene2_screen24.text: Julie yawned — half from the wine, half from emotional exhaustion.

scene2_screen25.text: Alright, that’s it. I’m claiming sanctuary in my room before someone puts on a board game or starts a political debate.

scene2_screen27.text: She raised an eyebrow, but didn’t say no. Upstairs, the house creaked like it too was tipsy.

scene2_screen28.text: Julie flicked on the bedside lamp. The room looked almost the same, like it had been waiting for her. She sat on the bed with a sigh, curling her legs under her. Patrick hovered near the door, unsure.

scene2_screen30.text: Only if you promise not to mock the poster.

scene2_screen31.text: (grinning) No promises. But I will respect the sanctity of boy band devotion.

scene2_screen32.text: He stepped inside. Sat on the floor, back against the bed. Close, but not too close. A pause. Not awkward. Just... full.

scene2_screen33.text: (quietly) I kept your book. The one you left at my place. With the angry little Post-it notes on every page?

scene2_screen34.text: (snorting) That’s how I flirt. Through passive-aggressive literary commentary.

scene2_screen35.text: It worked. Took me three chapters to fall for you. Five to realize I was already in too deep. And by chapter twelve, I was terrified.

scene2_screen37.text: Of not being enough. Of you figuring out I was faking it more than I was making it.

scene2_screen38.text: Julie didn’t speak. She reached down and gently touched his shoulder — just fingertips, just a second — but it said enough.

scene2_screen39.text: (soft) I was scared, too. Of losing myself. Of needing someone who didn’t know how to stay.

scene2_screen40.text: Patrick tilted his head to look up at her.

scene2_screen41.text: (smiling faintly) I never stopped caring. I just got bad at showing it.

scene2_screen42.text: Julie looked away. At the stars still clinging to the ceiling. In the past, layered in posters and pillows. Then back at him. At the man who once broke her heart with silence, and now was filling it with too much softness.

scene2_screen43.text: Do you ever wonder... if we had just taken one more breath before ending it?

scene2_screen45.text: Neither of them moved. But something between them did. Shifted. Reached. Held.

scene2_screen46.text: Downstairs, someone laughed too loudly at a bad joke. Upstairs, Julie and Patrick sat in the hush between years.

scene2_screen47.text: The kind of quiet where new beginnings start.

scene3_screen1.text: Julie sat curled up on the old couch, blanket over her knees, cocoa in one hand, nerves in the other.

scene3_screen2.text: Patrick was next to her, close enough to count the freckles near her collarbone if he dared. He didn’t. Yet.

scene3_screen4.text: I liked the idea of New Year’s. Clean slates. Sparkly dresses. Lies we tell ourselves with glitter.

scene3_screen6.text: (raising her mug) Cheers to personal growth.

scene3_screen7.text: Silence again. The comfortable kind. Julie looked at the fireplace, then at Patrick.

scene3_screen8.text: He was watching her. Not in that I-want-to-kiss-you way. In the I-already-did-and-I-might-never-stop kind of way. Which was, frankly, rude.

scene3_screen9.text: (quietly) I know this whole night’s been weird. I didn’t expect to walk into your life like this. But I also didn’t expect to still want to stay.

scene3_screen10.text: Julie blinked. Her fingers tightened around the cocoa mug. The clock on the wall blinked 11:59.

scene3_screen11.text: (half-whisper) You know I don’t do recycled resolutions.

scene3_screen12.text: Then don’t call it that. Call it… unfinished business.

scene3_choice1.text: What do you do as the clock strikes midnight?

opts.text: Kiss him. Like, really kiss him
Lean on his shoulder — warm, but cautious
Stand, walk to the window, and choose yourself

scene3_choice1_option1_screen1.text: Julie set the mug down. The TV in the background began counting: “Ten… nine…”

scene3_choice1_option1_screen2.text: She leaned in. He met her halfway.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen3.text: The kiss was unhurried, familiar, and somehow brand new. The kind that says, "I remember everything and still want more."

scene3_choice1_option1_screen4.text: The TV presenter said the cherished words.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen5.text: Outside, fireworks exploded. Inside, so did a few long-repressed feelings.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen6.text: (against her lips) I think this is my favorite midnight.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen7.text: It’s definitely top three… Okay, top one.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen8.text: (softly, still close) I forgot what this felt like.  And I didn’t know I missed it this much.

scene4_choice0_option1_screen11.text: Julie sits curled in a velvet armchair, a latte in one hand, her boots half off, one foot tucked under her. Across from her, Patrick leans over a small table, reading out loud from a beat-up copy of the book she once left behind.

scene4_choice0_option1_screen12.text: (reading, grinning) “Note to self,” she wrote in the margin. "If this man doesn’t cry at chapter fourteen, he’s emotionally unqualified.”Harsh.

scene4_choice0_option1_screen14.text: She reached over, stole one of his biscotti with shameless precision. He let her. Of course he did.

scene4_choice0_option1_screen15.text: They weren’t perfect. Still argued over what counted as "real" pizza. Still disagreed about how many throw pillows were necessary for a couch. But they both showed up now. Fully.

scene4_choice0_option1_screen16.text: No ghosting. No running. Just… growing.

scene4_choice0_option1_screen17.text: Later that evening, as they walk out of the bookstore hand in hand.

scene4_choice0_option1_screen18.text: Outside, twinkle lights line the windows. An old man in a Santa hat sells roasted chestnuts, and someone sings off-key carols nearby.

scene4_choice0_option1_screen19.text: They pause under the café awning. Hanging above them: a sprig of mistletoe, taped to the door frame with a Post-it that reads “Management takes no responsibility for romantic complications.”

scene4_choice0_option1_screen20.text: (looking up) You think it’s a trap?

scene4_choice0_option1_screen21.text: If it is, it’s a very on-brand one.

scene4_choice0_option1_screen22.text: He stepped closer. This time, she didn’t hesitate. Not even a little.

scene4_choice0_option1_screen24.text: They walked off into the evening. Not a perfect love story. But finally, one that made sense.

scene4_choice0_option1_screen25.text: New year. New rules. Maybe even…

scene4_choice0_option1_screen26.text: ✨ THE END ✨ Or is it the beginning…?

scene4_screen1.text: Julie exhaled and gently rested her head on Patrick’s shoulder. He stilled — then leaned his cheek lightly against her hair.

scene4_screen2.text: The clock struck midnight. Fireworks lit up the sky through the frosty window.

scene4_screen4.text: Let’s just… see where this goes. No promises. No pressure.

scene4_screen5.text: (half-whispering) Just… don’t disappear again.  I don’t think I’d laugh it off twice.

scene4_screen6.text: He nodded. And smiled. Like a man who didn’t need a promise to hope anyway.

scene4_choice0_option3_screen1.text: Julie stood. Walked to the window. Watched the fireworks go off in the distance, silent behind glass.

scene4_choice0_option3_screen2.text: She didn’t turn when she spoke.

scene4_choice0_option3_screen3.text: You’ll always matter to me. But maybe some love stories stay in the past for a reason.

scene4_choice0_option3_screen4.text: Behind her, Patrick rose too. He didn’t try to stop her.

scene4_choice0_option3_screen5.text: (quietly) Then I’m glad I got one last chapter. Even if it’s the epilogue.

scene4_choice0_option3_screen6.text: Julie smiled — not sad. Just… free.

scene4_choice0_option3_screen7.text: As Patrick turned to leave, something slipped from his coat pocket.  The familiar worn spine — her book. Still dog-eared, still wrapped in neon post-its that screamed in all caps. Still his.

scene4_choice0_option3_screen8.text: Julie blinked.  She didn’t say anything.  But her hand brushed the cover as he walked past, slower than he had to.

scene4_screen7.text: The fire burned low. Outside, the world exploded in color and sound. Inside, something changed. Rekindled. Reclaimed. Or released.

scene4_screen8.text: New year. New rules. Maybe even… a second chance.

scene4_screen9.text: ✨ THE END ✨Or is it the beginning…?
